About.title: A first for Pakistan
About.lead: The Pakistan Society Of Vascular Anomaly is a national, non-profit community connecting families, specialists, and centres to make expert care reachable everywhere.
About.missionBody: To raise awareness, end stigma, and ensure every person with a vascular anomaly in Pakistan can find timely, expert, multidisciplinary care.
About.visionBody: A Pakistan where a vascular anomaly diagnosis is met with clarity and compassion — not confusion, delay, or shame.
About.storyBody: Care exists in a handful of centres, but families across the country struggle to reach it. There has been no national voice — until now. PSOVA brings that voice, and a map to the help that already exists.
About.teamLead: A multidisciplinary board of clinicians, researchers, and family advocates.
About.partnersLead: We align our information with global standards and work alongside leading Pakistani institutions.

WhatAreVA.title: What are vascular anomalies?
WhatAreVA.lead: Conditions in which blood or lymphatic vessels form or grow abnormally. They are not contagious, not cancerous, and not caused by anything a parent did.
WhatAreVA.defBody: "Vascular" means blood vessels; an "anomaly" means something developed differently from usual. They can appear as a mark or lump on the skin, or lie deeper in muscle, bone, or organs. Most appear at or shortly after birth and range from harmless birthmarks to conditions needing specialist care.
WhatAreVA.tumorsBody: Growths made of cells that multiply — like infantile hemangioma. They often appear after birth, grow, then shrink.
WhatAreVA.malformationsBody: Vessels that formed incorrectly but do not multiply — like a port-wine stain. Usually present from birth and persistent, growing with the child.
WhatAreVA.classificationLead: The globally accepted system doctors use to name and group these conditions, so a patient gets a consistent diagnosis anywhere in the world.
WhatAreVA.keyPointBody: A tumour tends to appear, grow, then shrink. A malformation is usually there from birth, does not go away on its own, and grows in proportion with the child.
WhatAreVA.ctaBody: Clear, reassuring guides to the most common vascular anomalies.

Patients.title: You have found the right place
Patients.lead: A new diagnosis can be frightening. Here is what it means, what helps, and how to find care.
Patients.step1Body: The vast majority of vascular anomalies are not cancerous and are manageable.
Patients.step2Body: An experienced specialist can identify the exact type and what (if anything) to do.
Patients.step3Body: The best care brings several specialists together. Use our directory to find one.
Patients.treatmentBody: There is no single treatment — care is matched to the type, size, and location. Options include active monitoring, medicines (such as propranolol or sirolimus), laser, sclerotherapy, embolization, and surgery — often combined.
Patients.askLead: Have a question about a birthmark or diagnosis? Send it to our panel and we'll point you in the right direction.
Patients.supportBody: You are not alone. Connecting with families on the same journey changes everything — from isolation to understanding.
Patients.costBody: Much care in Pakistan is paid out of pocket. We share guidance on hospital zakat/charity funds and what programmes like Sehat Sahulat may cover.
Patients.schoolBody: Practical tips for school, sport, clothing, and answering questions with confidence.
Patients.stigmaBody: Birthmarks are not anyone's fault and not contagious. Compassion and accurate information protect a child's confidence.

Registry.title: Counted. Cared for.
Registry.lede: Pakistan's first national picture of vascular anomalies. Families and clinicians enrol cases, PSOVA verifies them, and the nation gets anonymised statistics — while every patient's identity stays encrypted and protected.
Registry.whyBody: Pakistan has no national dataset of vascular anomaly patients. A registry reveals how common these conditions are, guides research and services, and helps families find the right care.
Registry.whoBody: Any family affected by a vascular anomaly can enrol — no account needed. Doctors can register to submit structured clinical cases on behalf of their patients.
Registry.privacyBody: Your identity is encrypted at rest with AES-256. We only publish anonymised counts. You can ask us to remove your record at any time.
Registry.clinicianStrip: Are you a doctor? Register to submit structured cases (ISSVA classification) and track your submissions.
Registry.consent1Q: What information do you store, and how is it protected?
Registry.consent1A: We store the details you provide — name, guardian name, CNIC, phone, email, address, date of birth, and condition details. All identifying information is encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. The database never holds your identity in readable form, and only authorised PSOVA verification staff can view a record — every such view is logged.
Registry.consent2A: Only PSOVA’s verification staff (a small, accountable team) and, if a clinician submitted your case, your treating clinician for their own case. The public only ever sees anonymised totals — never any individual record.
Registry.consent3A: To build a national registry of vascular anomaly cases and to publish anonymised statistics and research that improve care across Pakistan. We do not sell data or use third-party analytics on registry pages.
Registry.consent4Q: What are my rights, and how long do you keep my data?
Registry.consent4A: You can request correction or complete removal of your record at any time. We keep your record until you ask us to remove it. To exercise these rights, contact PSOVA on +92 321 4261 950 or by email.
Registry.disclaimer: The registry is not a medical service and does not provide diagnosis or treatment. For any medical concern, consult a qualified specialist.

mdt.newLede: Describe the case without anything that could identify the patient: no names, contact details, hospital numbers, exact dates of birth or photos showing faces.
mdt.empty: No posts yet. Be the first to post a case.
mdt.readOnly: Your membership has lapsed, so posting is paused.
mdt.error: That could not be completed. Please try again.
mdt.warning: Never include names, phone numbers, CNIC, hospital numbers or other identifiers. Posts are visible to doctors at every registered centre.
mdt.summaryHint: What was found, what has been tried, and what you would like the group's view on.
mdt.attach: Attach files (only files marked for teaching can be attached)
mdt.confirm: I confirm this post contains nothing that could identify the patient, and any attached files show no identifying features.

support.title: Patient support fund
support.lede: Ask PSOVA to raise money for a patient who cannot afford treatment. PSOVA reviews every request and shows approved ones publicly without anything that identifies the patient.
support.empty: No requests yet. Open a patient and choose "Request help from the patient support fund".
support.readOnly: Your membership has lapsed, so new requests are paused.
support.warning: The case description is shown publicly once PSOVA approves it. Never include names, phone numbers, CNIC, hospital numbers, the family's exact address or a photo.
support.costHint: The total cost of the treatment the fund is asked to cover.
support.blurbHint: For example: age group, the condition in plain words, why treatment matters, and what the family can and cannot contribute.
support.confirm: The family agreed to ask for support, and this text contains nothing that could identify the patient or family.
support.alreadyOpen: This patient already has an open request.
support.error: That could not be submitted. Please check the details.

reports.title: Reports
reports.lede: Counts for your centre only. They contain no patient details.

tiersInfo.MEMBER: Registered and verified by PSOVA: listed in the directory, with a registration certificate and a dashboard.
tiersInfo.ACCREDITED: PSOVA has reviewed the centre's credentials and team, and the centre keeps its records and follow-ups active.
tiersInfo.EXCELLENCE: A multidisciplinary centre with a high case volume that shares cases with NVAR and takes part in the case board.

SupportFund.metaDescription: Help families in Pakistan pay for vascular anomaly treatment. Every case is verified by PSOVA and shown without anything that identifies the patient.
SupportFund.title: Help a child get the treatment they need
SupportFund.lead: Treatment for a vascular anomaly can cost more than a family can afford. Registered PSOVA centres bring us cases, PSOVA verifies each one, and your gift goes to the treatment itself.
SupportFund.step1: A PSOVA centre's doctor identifies a patient who cannot afford treatment and submits a request.
SupportFund.step2: PSOVA reviews it. Cases are shown here without names or anything that could identify the family.
SupportFund.step3: You give by bank or wallet and quote the case code. PSOVA records every gift and pays the treatment.
SupportFund.raised: {amount} raised so far, helping {count, plural, =1 {1 patient} other {# patients}}.
SupportFund.empty: There are no cases open right now. Please check back soon, or give to PSOVA's general fund.
SupportFund.giveBody: Use any account below and write the case code (for example SF-1A2B3C4D) in the transfer reference, so we can match your gift. Without a code, your gift supports the fund as a whole.
